title: Speaking Part 1 — growing an answer
note:
The unit here is a DISCOURSE MOVE, not a clause. Part 1 does not fail candidates on grammar; it fails them on stopping after four words. So a level is one more move, and the moves are the four an examiner is listening for.

Every level is written in full by a person. The page never composes an answer — it only chooses which level to show, and diffs one level against the next to know what was added. That rule is taken from clause-builder.json and it is the reason this file can be checked by eye.

Each voice runs the same ladder at the same depth, so switching voice mid-build keeps the student's position and only changes whose life it is. Three voices, because 'I moved in right after I started my current job' is unusable to a fifteen-year-old, and unusable input is not input.
